description: Influencer dashboard (read views) plus the message-status and email data model it depends on. The dashboard shows upcoming sessions, past sessions, earnings, and per-booking message status. Phases 4 (messaging) and 5 (reminders) are NOT implemented, so there is no Message table yet; this feature introduces a lightweight messages/notifications model and a structured-log email sender (mirroring lib/alerts.ts) so the dashboard has real data to display and the Phase 6 'email receipt/confirmation' task has a home. There is no auth yet, so the dashboard is reached via the same signed-link pattern used by the Google connect flow (lib/signing.ts / buildConnectUrl). Depends on FEAT-002 (shared-event fields) because the dashboard reads session event/meet data. Message status + email sending here are consumed by FEAT-004 manual actions.
steps: Schema + migration: add a Message model to prisma/schema.prisma to record outbound customer communications (confirmation, receipt, reminder, link-resent) with at least: id, bookingId (FK, onDelete Cascade), channel String (e.g. 'email'|'whatsapp'|'sms'|'log'), template String, status String (e.g. 'queued'|'sent'|'failed'), error String?, sentAt DateTime?, createdAt/updatedAt, and an index on bookingId. Follow the @map snake_case + enum/String conventions already in the file. Add a hand-written migration prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_messages/migration.sql in the existing SQL style, timestamp after FEAT-002's migration.

Create lib/email.ts following the lib/alerts.ts delivery-hook pattern: an EmailSender type with a default logSender that writes a structured console line (no real SMTP in this environment / Phase 4), a setEmailSender override hook, and a sendBookingEmail(bookingId, kind) that renders a receipt/confirmation from the booking + payment + session + service and records a Message row (status 'sent' for the log sender). Keep it dependency-free (no new npm packages).

Wire message-status recording so the dashboard has data: when the confirmation message is enqueued/sent in the meeting flow (lib/meeting.ts enqueueSendMessage path), and when the email receipt is sent, create/update a Message row. Do this without introducing a real Phase 4 worker; a thin recording helper in lib/messages.ts (createMessage/markMessageSent/markMessageFailed) is enough. If adding the recording inside createMeetingForBooking, keep it best-effort and non-throwing like alerts.

Dashboard access: add a signed-link helper (reuse lib/signing.ts) e.g. buildDashboardUrl(influencerId) with its own purpose string, analogous to buildConnectUrl in lib/google-tokens.ts. Add a script scripts/dashboard-link.ts mirroring scripts/connect-link.ts to print the link, and a package.json script (e.g. "dashboard:link") mirroring "google:connect-link". The dashboard route must verify the signed token (verifyToken) before showing anything; an invalid/expired token returns 403, matching app/api/google/connect/route.ts.

Create the dashboard page under app/dashboard/ (App Router server component, `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, Prisma via lib/db.ts). It takes the signed token (e.g. ?t=...), resolves the influencer, and renders: Upcoming sessions (future sessions with their bookings, seats filled vs capacity, meet_link, each booking's status and latest message status), Past sessions (completed/elapsed), Earnings (sum of CAPTURED payments, grouped sensibly e.g. total and per-service, formatted with the currency like BookingFlow's formatPrice), and a message-status column. Reuse the CSS classes in app/globals.css (card, muted, choice, slot, primary) rather than adding a new design system. Keep interactive bits (the manual-action buttons from FEAT-004) in a client component similar to app/[influencer]/book/BookingFlow.tsx.

Keep the dashboard read-only in this feature; the manual-action buttons and management forms are FEAT-004. Leave clear seams (e.g. pass the signed token / booking ids to a client component) so FEAT-004 can attach actions without restructuring.

Add tests where they can be pure: e.g. tests/earnings.test.ts asserting the earnings aggregation helper (extract the sum/group logic into a pure function in lib/dashboard.ts) over a fixture array of payments, in the node:test + tsx style. Avoid DB-dependent tests; if a query helper needs Prisma, keep the pure math separate and test only that.

Update doc/06-groups-and-dashboard.md to check off the 'Dashboard' and 'Email receipt/confirmation' tasks (email sending lands here; manual actions and management are FEAT-004). Note in the doc that email/WhatsApp delivery is still a structured-log stub pending Phases 4/5.
acceptance_criteria: prisma/schema.prisma has a Message model with a matching hand-written SQL migration (timestamp after FEAT-002)
lib/email.ts exists with a setEmailSender hook and a default structured-log sender, mirroring lib/alerts.ts, and records a Message row when sending a receipt/confirmation

The dashboard at app/dashboard renders upcoming sessions, past sessions, earnings (sum of CAPTURED payments formatted by currency), and per-booking message status, reading real Prisma data including the shared group meet_link
The dashboard is gated by a signed, expiring token verified with lib/signing.ts; an invalid/expired token yields 403
scripts/dashboard-link.ts and a package.json script print a working signed dashboard link, mirroring the connect-link flow
A pure earnings-aggregation function is unit-tested in tests/ without a live DB
verification: Static validation: grep that app/dashboard imports resolve to real exports (lib/db, lib/signing verifyToken, lib/dashboard helpers, lib/email) and that every Prisma field referenced (Message.*, Payment.status CAPTURED, Session.eventId/meetLink, Booking.status) matches prisma/schema.prisma
Confirm the new migration column/table names exactly match the Prisma model @map names
Read the dashboard server component and confirm it returns 403 on a bad token before any data is shown, matching app/api/google/connect/route.ts
In a normal environment: `npx prisma generate`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (CI-only here; note in findings)

findings.summary: Built the read-only influencer dashboard plus the Message data model and structured-log email sender it depends on. All work validated statically (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox: no npm/prisma/tsc/next/tsx), except the pure earnings aggregation whose exact outputs were verified by running the logic in plain node.
findings.schema_and_migration: prisma/schema.prisma gained a Message model: id, bookingId @map("booking_id") FK onDelete Cascade, channel, template, status (default 'queued'), error?, sentAt? @map("sent_at"), createdAt/updatedAt, @@index([bookingId]), @@map("messages"). Booking gained a messages Message[] relation. Hand-written migration prisma/migrations/20261011000000_messages/migration.sql (timestamp later than FEAT-002's 20261010000000) CREATE TABLE messages + CREATE INDEX messages_booking_id_idx + FK to bookings ON DELETE CASCADE, mirroring the 20261009000000 style. migration_lock.toml provider unchanged. Verified column names (booking_id, sent_at, created_at, updated_at) and the index name match the Prisma @map names / default index naming used in prior migrations.
findings.email: lib/email.ts mirrors lib/alerts.ts: EmailSender type, default logSender (structured console line, NO SMTP), setEmailSender override hook, and sendBookingEmail(bookingId, kind: 'booking-confirmation'|'receipt') that loads booking+session+service+influencer+latest CAPTURED payment, renders a confirmation/receipt, calls the sender, and records a Message row (channel 'email') via lib/messages helpers. Best-effort/non-throwing like alerts: records 'queued' then markMessageSent on success, markMessageFailed on error. Dependency-free (uses Intl for currency formatting).
findings.messages_helpers: lib/messages.ts: createMessage/markMessageSent/markMessageFailed. All best-effort and non-throwing (try/catch -> console.error, return null/no-op) so recording never fails the booking/meeting job. MessageChannel/MessageStatus string unions match the schema's documented values.
findings.confirmation_wiring: lib/meeting.ts: added enqueueConfirmation(deps, bookingId) that records a 'queued' Message row (channel 'whatsapp', template 'booking-confirmation') via createMessage (non-throwing) then calls deps.enqueueSendMessage. Both prior enqueueSendMessage call sites (already-scheduled re-enqueue, and the scheduled success path) now call enqueueConfirmation. No behavioural change to meeting creation; the recording cannot throw. The existing tests/group-meeting.test.ts mocks @/lib/db; since createMessage swallows errors, that test's enqueue assertions are unaffected even if the stub lacks message.create.
findings.signed_link: lib/dashboard.ts exports DASHBOARD_LINK_PURPOSE ('influencer-dashboard-link', distinct from CONNECT_LINK_PURPOSE) and buildDashboardUrl(influencerId, ttlSec=7d) using signToken, analogous to buildConnectUrl in lib/google-tokens.ts; it points at /dashboard?t=... scripts/dashboard-link.ts mirrors scripts/connect-link.ts (dotenv/config, resolve slug, print link). package.json gained "dashboard:link": "tsx scripts/dashboard-link.ts" next to "google:connect-link".
findings.dashboard_page: app/dashboard/page.tsx is an App Router server component (export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic', Prisma via @/lib/db). It verifyToken(DASHBOARD_LINK_PURPOSE, ?t=) BEFORE loading any data; invalid/expired -> renders a 403 message (influencer-not-found -> 404), matching the gate-first pattern of app/api/google/connect/route.ts. It loads the influencer's sessions (with service + visible bookings PAID/SCHEDULED/COMPLETED/CANCELLED/FAILED + latest Message), splits upcoming (endTime>=now) vs past, computes seatsFilled vs capacity, and loads CAPTURED payments. Earnings are aggregated by the pure lib/dashboard.aggregateEarnings and the whole view is handed to a client component.
findings.client_component: app/dashboard/Dashboard.tsx ('use client') renders Earnings (total per currency + per-service, formatted with Intl currency like BookingFlow's formatPrice), Upcoming sessions, Past sessions, each booking's status + latest message status + per-booking/shared meet_link + lastError. Reuses globals.css classes (main/h1/h2/card/muted/error). READ-ONLY this feature; the signed token and booking ids are passed into DashboardData as explicit seams so FEAT-004 can attach manual-action buttons without restructuring.
findings.earnings_pure_fn_and_test: aggregateEarnings in lib/dashboard.ts is a pure function (no DB/Prisma types): sums totalsByCurrency and byService (per service+currency, with count), each sorted amount-desc then name. tests/earnings.test.ts (node:test + tsx style) covers single-currency total, per-service grouping+order, mixed-currency separation, and empty input. Because tsx is unavailable here, the exact aggregation outputs were verified by running the identical logic in plain node (env -u NODE_OPTIONS) and they matched the test's deepEqual expectations.
findings.docs: doc/06-groups-and-dashboard.md: checked off 'Dashboard' and 'Email receipt/confirmation'; added a 'Dashboard (read-only)' section (signed-link access, 403 gate, what it shows, read-only + FEAT-004 seams) and an 'Email receipt/confirmation' section noting email/WhatsApp delivery is still a structured-log stub pending Phases 4/5.
findings.validation_ci_only: CI-only (could NOT run in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox): npx prisma generate, npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), next build, and npm test via tsx (needs node_modules + @/* alias). tests/earnings.test.ts runs in CI; its math was separately confirmed in plain node here. Static validation performed: read every new/changed file for TS correctness; grep-confirmed verifyToken/signToken, buildDashboardUrl/DASHBOARD_LINK_PURPOSE/aggregateEarnings, createMessage/markMessageSent/markMessageFailed, sendBookingEmail/setEmailSender are exported and used correctly; confirmed every Prisma field/enum referenced (Message.* and its @map names, Payment.status CAPTURED, Session.eventId/meetLink, Booking.status/meetLink/lastError, Booking.messages relation) matches prisma/schema.prisma and that the new migration column/index/table names match the model.
findings.deviations: Earnings total is returned per-currency (totalsByCurrency) rather than a single scalar, because a dashboard may legitimately mix currencies and collapsing them would be wrong; per-service rows are keyed by (serviceId, currency) for the same reason. buildDashboardUrl + DASHBOARD_LINK_PURPOSE live in lib/dashboard.ts (alongside the aggregation) rather than lib/google-tokens.ts, keeping dashboard concerns together while still reusing lib/signing.ts.
